fullPassage: At a rich merchant's house, there was a birthday party for the merchant's son, and the children of rich and great people were there. Among them was a handsome boy, the son of the editor of a newspaper. He said, "My dad can put everybody's dad in the newspaper. People are afraid of him, my mom says, because he can do whatever he wants with the paper." "But my dad can buy a hundred dollars' worth of candy, and give it to children. Can your dad do that?" asked the merchant's son. "And those whose names end in 'sen' can never be anything at all," he continued. The editor's son was very angry at what he had said, for his father's name was Petersen. But outside the door was a poor boy. His status was so low that he was not even allowed to enter the room. The boy was there to help with the party, and the merchant's son told him to stand behind the door and wait for his call. There he stood, watching the well-dressed children having such a good time inside. "Oh, if I could be one of them," he thought. Then he heard what the merchant's son said about names, and what he said was enough to make him even more unhappy. His parents back home did not even have a penny to buy a newspaper, and worse, his father's name, and of course his own, ended in "sen." But he was born into the world, and the station of life was chosen for him, so he had to be satisfied. And this is what happened that night. Many years passed, and the children grew up. There stood a splendid house in the town. It was much bigger and fancier than the one where the merchant's son had had his birthday party long ago. Which of the children we talked about could say this house was his own? The house belonged to the poor little boy who had stood behind the door that night. He really had become something great, although his name ended in "sen."

questions.passage: At a rich merchant's house, there was a birthday party for the merchant's son, and the children of rich and great people were there. Among them was a handsome boy, the son of the editor of a newspaper. He said, "My dad can put everybody's dad in the newspaper. People are afraid of him, my mom says, because he can do whatever he wants with the paper." "But my dad can buy a hundred dollars' worth of candy, and give it to children. Can your dad do that?" asked the merchant's son. "And those whose names end in 'sen' can never be anything at all," he continued. The editor's son was very angry at what he had said, for his father's name was Petersen. But outside the door was a poor boy. His status was so low that he was not even allowed to enter the room. The boy was there to help with the party, and the merchant's son told him to stand behind the door and wait for his call. There he stood, watching the well-dressed children having such a good time inside. "Oh, if I could be one of them," he thought. Then he heard what the merchant's son said about names, and what he said was enough to make him even more unhappy. His parents back home did not even have a penny to buy a newspaper, and worse, his father's name, and of course his own, ended in "sen." But he was born into the world, and the station of life was chosen for him, so he had to be satisfied. And this is what happened that night. Many years passed, and the children grew up. There stood a splendid house in the town. It was much bigger and fancier than the one where the merchant's son had had his birthday party long ago. Which of the children we talked about could say this house was his own? The house belonged to the poor little boy who had stood behind the door that night. He really had become something great, although his name ended in "sen."

구문 분석: the children of rich and great people(주어: ~의 아이들) + were(동사) + there(거기에). 'of + 명사'가 the children을 뒤에서 수식한다. rich and great이 people을 함께 수식.

단어 순서: the → children → of → rich → and → great → people → were → there (9단어).
det.tip: the children of ~ = ~의 아이들. rich and great people=부유하고 지체 높은 사람들.

questions.wa: the children of rich and great people were there
accept: the children of rich and great people were there

questions.passage: At a rich merchant's house, there was a birthday party for the merchant's son, and the children of rich and great people were there. Among them was a handsome boy, the son of the editor of a newspaper. He said, "My dad can put everybody's dad in the newspaper. People are afraid of him, my mom says, because he can do whatever he wants with the paper." "But my dad can buy a hundred dollars' worth of candy, and give it to children. Can your dad do that?" asked the merchant's son. "And those whose names end in 'sen' can never be anything at all," he continued. The editor's son was very angry at what he had said, for his father's name was Petersen. But outside the door was a poor boy. His status was so low that he was not even allowed to enter the room. The boy was there to help with the party, and the merchant's son told him to stand behind the door and wait for his call. There he stood, watching the well-dressed children having such a good time inside. "Oh, if I could be one of them," he thought. Then he heard what the merchant's son said about names, and what he said was enough to make him even more unhappy. His parents back home did not even have a penny to buy a newspaper, and worse, his father's name, and of course his own, ended in "sen." But he was born into the world, and the station of life was chosen for him, so he had to be satisfied. And this is what happened that night. Many years passed, and the children grew up. There stood a splendid house in the town. __________ where the merchant's son had had his birthday party long ago. Which of the children we talked about could say this house was his own? The house belonged to the poor little boy who had stood behind the door that night. He really had become something great, although his name ended in "sen."
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [보기]의 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.
'그것은 그 집보다 훨씬 더 크고 화려했다.'
[보기] and, bigger, fancier, It, much, one, than, the, was
(9단어, 영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 본문: 'It was much bigger and fancier than the one' = 그것은 그 집보다 훨씬 더 크고 화려했다 (9단어)
det.analysis:
주어 It + was + much bigger and fancier(훨씬 더 크고 화려한) + than the one(그 집보다). much는 비교급 bigger/fancier를 강조하는 부사. than the one에서 the one은 비교 대상(옛 집).

단어 순서: It → was → much → bigger → and → fancier → than → the → one (9단어).
det.tip: much + 비교급 = 훨씬 더 ~한. bigger and fancier than the one=그 집보다 더 크고 화려한.

questions.wa: It was much bigger and fancier than the one

questions.stem:
다음 우리말을 [조건]에 맞게 영작하시오. (영어로)
우리말: 그래서 그는 만족해야만 했다.
[조건] (1) be, had, he, satisfied, so, to를 모두 사용할 것
(2) 정확히 6단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: so he had to be satisfied(그래서 그는 만족해야만 했다)
det.analysis:
구문 분석: so(그래서) + he(주어) + had to(~해야만 했다) + be satisfied(만족하다). have to의 과거형 had to 뒤에 동사원형 be가 오고, be satisfied는 '만족하다'라는 수동형 표현.

단어 순서: so → he → had → to → be → satisfied (6단어).
det.tip: had to + 동사원형 = ~해야만 했다. be satisfied=만족하다. so he had to be satisfied.

questions.wa: so he had to be satisfied
accept: so he had to be satisfied
